bank.q: Look! The children ___ in the park.
bank.why: Look! menandakan kejadian sekarang: are/is + verb-ing. Children jamak, jadi are playing.

bank.q: There ___ two books on the table.
bank.why: Two books jamak, jadi There are.

bank.q: My class starts ___ 8 o'clock.
bank.why: Untuk jam tepat dipakai at.

bank.q: The opposite of "early" is ___.
bank.why: Lawan kata early (awal/pagi) adalah late (terlambat).

bank.q: Where are Tom and Lisa? I cannot see ___.
bank.why: Sebagai objek verb see dipakai them.

bank.q: I ___ drink coffee at night, because I cannot sleep after that.
bank.why: Karena tidak bisa tidur setelahnya, masuk akal kalau never (tidak pernah).

bank.q: ___ do you go to school? By bus.
bank.why: Jawaban menyebut cara (by bus), jadi pertanyaannya How.

bank.q: A ___ is a place where we buy medicine.
bank.why: Pharmacy = apotek. Library = perpustakaan, bakery = toko roti.

bank.q: I do not have ___ money.
bank.why: Money tidak bisa dihitung, jadi much. Many dan a few untuk benda yang bisa dihitung.

bank.q: We use a ___ to eat soup.
bank.why: Spoon = sendok, dipakai untuk makan sup.

bank.q: You are coming to the party, ___?
bank.why: Kalimat positif dengan are diikuti tag negatif: aren't you?

bank.q: I ___ my keys while I was running for the bus.
bank.why: Kejadian singkat di masa lalu yang terjadi saat kegiatan lain berlangsung: past simple (lost).

bank.q: You ___ park here. It is forbidden.
bank.why: Mustn't = dilarang. Don't have to dan needn't = tidak perlu.

bank.q: Is there ___ sugar in the tea?
bank.why: Pertanyaan dengan benda tak terhitung (sugar) memakai any.

bank.q: Please turn ___ the music. It is too loud.
bank.why: Turn down = mengecilkan volume.

bank.q: If I ___ a car, I would drive to work.
bank.why: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + verb.

bank.q: Mount Everest is ___ mountain in the world.
bank.why: Superlative memakai the + adjective-est: the highest.

bank.q: She is afraid ___ spiders.
bank.why: Kolokasi tetap: afraid of.

bank.q: He is a very ___ driver. He never has accidents.
bank.why: Sebelum kata benda (driver) dipakai adjective: careful.

bank.q: She plays ___ guitar very well.
bank.why: Untuk alat musik yang dimainkan dipakai the.

bank.q: After the long meeting, we decided to call it a ___.
bank.why: Idiom call it a day = berhenti bekerja untuk hari ini.

bank.q: He is believed ___ the country last night.
bank.why: Last night menunjukkan masa lalu, jadi perfect infinitive: to have left.

bank.q: I am exhausted. I ___ since six this morning.
bank.why: Since + titik waktu dan masih berlanjut: present perfect continuous.

bank.q: If I had studied medicine, I ___ a doctor now.
bank.why: Syarat di masa lalu, akibat sekarang (now): would + verb.

bank.q: ___ unemployed need more support during a recession.
bank.why: The + adjective dipakai untuk kelompok orang: the unemployed.

bank.q: The company decided to ___ a new strategy.
bank.why: Adopt = menerapkan. Adapt = menyesuaikan, adept = mahir.

bank.q: He is very talented. ___, he is extremely humble.
bank.why: Moreover = lagipula, menambah informasi positif.

bank.q: The company is responsible ___ the delay.
bank.why: Kolokasi tetap: responsible for.

bank.q: The man ___ car was stolen called the police.
bank.why: Whose menyatakan kepemilikan: mobil milik pria itu.

bank.q: The heavy rain had a bad ___ on the crops.
bank.why: Effect = dampak (kata benda). Affect adalah kata kerja.

bank.q: After years in Jakarta, I am used to ___ in traffic.
bank.why: Be used to + verb-ing = sudah terbiasa.

bank.q: He worked ___ hard that he became ill.
bank.why: So + adjective/adverb + that = begitu ... sehingga ...

bank.q: I suggest that he ___ a doctor about his cough.
bank.why: Setelah suggest that dipakai bentuk dasar verb (subjunctive): see.

bank.q: You ___ have told me earlier! Now it is too late.
bank.why: Should have + past participle = seharusnya (menyesalkan hal yang tidak dilakukan).

bank.q: Rarely ___ such a talented performer.
bank.why: Adverbia negatif di awal kalimat membuat inversi: Rarely do we see.

bank.q: We would be grateful if you could ___ us with the details.
bank.why: Provide someone with something = memberikan (formal).

bank.q: ___ the exam, she felt relieved and went out with friends.
bank.why: Having passed = setelah lulus (aktif, selesai lebih dulu). Subjeknya she.

bank.q: I cannot stand him. He gets on my ___.
bank.why: Idiom get on someone's nerves = membuat kesal.

bank.q: The politician gave an ___ answer, avoiding the question.
bank.why: Evasive = mengelak. Explicit = tegas, honest = jujur.

bank.q: He is not experienced ___ to lead the team.
bank.why: Adjective + enough + to + verb = cukup ... untuk ...

articles.title: At the Bus Stop
body: Every morning, Ali waits at the bus stop near his house. The bus usually comes at seven fifteen. Today it is late.
An old man sits next to Ali. He has a small bag and a newspaper. They talk about the weather. The old man says it will rain in the afternoon.
At last the bus arrives. Ali helps the old man get on the bus. Then he takes a seat by the window and opens his book.

qs.q: What time does the bus usually come?
What does Ali do when the bus arrives?
opts: He helps the old man get on

articles.title: The Case for Walking
body: Walking is the simplest form of exercise, yet many people ignore it. It costs nothing, needs no equipment and can be done almost anywhere.

Studies suggest that a brisk thirty-minute walk each day lowers the risk of heart disease and improves mood. Walking outdoors also seems to help people think more creatively, perhaps because the mind is free to wander.
Of course, walking will not solve every health problem. However, for those who spend most of the day sitting, it is an easy first step towards a more active life.

qs.q: What is one advantage of walking?
opts: It must be done in a gym

qs.q: According to the studies, what does a daily brisk walk do?
opts: It lowers the risk of heart disease and improves mood

qs.q: Who is walking an easy first step for?
opts: People who sit most of the day
